ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle ABC=30^\circ$. Connect $AC$. Follow the steps below to draw: Take $C$ and $B$ as centers, and with the length of $BC$ as the radius, draw arcs. The arcs intersect at point $P$. Connect $BP$ and $CP$. What is the measure of $\angle ACP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} According to the steps given in the question, the diagram is completed as follows:\\
Since rhombus ABCD, $\angle$ABC=30$^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle$BCD=150$^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle$ACB=75$^\circ$,\\
(1) When point P is above BC,\\
since BP=PC=BC,\\
thus, $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore, $\angle$PCB=60$^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle$ACP=$\angle$ACB−$\angle$PCB=75$^\circ$−60$^\circ$=\boxed{15^\circ};\\
(2) When point P' is below BC,\\
since BP'=P'C=BC,\\
thus, $\triangle BP'C$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore, $\angle$P'CB=60$^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle$ACP'=$\angle$ACB+$\angle$P'CB=75$^\circ$+60$^\circ$=135$^\circ$,\\
In conclusion, the degree of $\angle$ACP is either $\boxed{15^\circ}$ or 135$^\circ$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, in the rhombus $ABCD$, $\angle ABC=30^\circ$. Connect $AC$. Then take $C$ and $B$ as centers, and with length $BC$ as the radius, draw arcs intersecting at point $P$. Connect $BP$ and $CP$. What is the measure of $\angle ACP$?
raw_record.answer: According to the steps given in the question, the diagram is completed as follows: Since $ABCD$ is a rhombus and $\angle ABC=30^\circ$, therefore $\angle BCD=150^\circ$, thus $\angle ACB=75^\circ$. (1) When point $P$ is above $BC$, since $BP=PC=BC$, $\triangle BPC$ is an equilateral triangle, so $\angle PCB=60^\circ$. Hence $\angle ACP=\angle ACB-\angle PCB=75^\circ-60^\circ=\boxed{15^\circ}$. (2) When point $P'$ is below $BC$, since $BP'=P'C=BC$, $\triangle BP'C$ is an equilateral triangle, so $\angle P'CB=60^\circ$. Hence $\angle ACP'=\angle ACB+\angle P'CB=75^\circ+60^\circ=135^\circ$. In conclusion, the measure of $\angle ACP$ is either $\boxed{15^\circ}$ or $135^\circ$.

Image description: In the figure is an obliquely placed rhombus/parallelogram ABCD, B and C are below, A and D are above, sides AB, BC, CD, DA form a quadrilateral, and diagonal AC has already been connected; the specific position of point P is not drawn in the figure.
Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rhombus, it is also a parallelogram, and adjacent interior angles are supplementary. Given ∠ABC = 30°, therefore ∠BCD = 180° - 30° = 150°. The diagonal AC of a rhombus bisects the angle at vertex C, so ∠ACB = 150° ÷ 2 = 75°. Also because arcs are drawn with B and C as centers and BC as radius, and the intersection point is P, so BP = CP = BC, triangle BPC is an equilateral triangle, therefore ∠PCB = 60°. Since the two equal-radius arcs with B and C as centers have two intersection points: if P and A are on the same side of BC, then ∠ACP = ∠ACB - ∠PCB = 75° - 60° = 15°; if P is on the other side of BC, then ∠ACP = ∠ACB + ∠PCB = 75° + 60° = 135°.
